phase3_findings.description: The try block in performTurn (ChatController.ts 394-440) covers processing of a successful answer (setConversationId 403, answerToMessages 406, update 411-414), not only sendMessage, and its catch treats every error as a failed turn: it logs '[RadChat] sendMessage failed:', shows the error bubble and, new in this diff, for a typed turn calls onTurnFailed, which refills the composer and re-stages attachments although the backend answered, inviting a duplicate send. Reachable errors: sourcesToMarkdown reading s.title on a null source (116), escapeMd on a non-string title (109), a non-array sources value with a length (115), or host.onConversationIdChange throwing. The broad try predates the PR; the diff gave its catch a 'retry this turn' meaning.

customRendererFor (blockGuards.ts 158-165, used at BlockRenderer.tsx 110-113) returns undefined for an own blockRenderers entry that is not a function, so BlockRenderer renders null with no log for blocks from sendMessage, getConversation or a command's replyBlocks; only appendBlocks warns (ChatWidget.tsx 531). Before this diff the same misconfiguration threw.

No test covers the unwrapChatbot(chatbotKit) call at ChatWidget.tsx 54: under vitest the default import is already the component, so restoring a plain default import of react-chatbot-kit would still pass every test; kitInterop.test.ts tests unwrapChatbot only in isolation and nothing imports the built package under Node ESM.

report:
## Verdict: REJECT (one Critical finding: a successful answer that fails to process is treated as a failed turn and offered for resend)

This PR is not ready to merge, because the failed-turn handling it adds can ask the user to resend a question the backend already answered.

Rule applied: rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🔴 Critical

1. `src/chat/ChatController.ts` lines 394-440: the `try` block in `performTurn` covers the processing of a successful answer, not only the `sendMessage` call, and its catch treats every error as a failed turn. When processing the answer throws, the user sees the error message although the backend answered. For a typed turn, the catch now also calls `onTurnFailed`, which puts the question back in the input and stages its attachments again, so the user is invited to send it twice. The log line `[RadChat] sendMessage failed:` is also wrong for these errors. Errors this can catch include: `sourcesToMarkdown` reading `s.title` on a `null` source entry (line 116), `escapeMd` called with a title that is not a string (line 109), a `sources` value that is not an array (line 115), and an error thrown by `host.onConversationIdChange` through `setConversationId` (line 403). The broad `try` existed before this PR; this diff gave its catch the new "retry this turn" meaning. (raised by 1/5 agents)

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

1. `src/blocks/blockGuards.ts` lines 158-165, used at `src/blocks/BlockRenderer.tsx` lines 110-113: a `blockRenderers` entry that is not a function is ignored with no log for blocks that arrive from `sendMessage`, `getConversation` or a command's `replyBlocks`. Only `appendBlocks` warns about such an entry (`src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx` line 531). Before this diff the same misconfiguration threw an error. (raised by 1/5 agents)
2. `src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx` line 54: no test covers the `unwrapChatbot(chatbotKit)` call. Under vitest the default import is already the component, so putting back a plain default import of `react-chatbot-kit` would still pass every test. The new `src/widget/kitInterop.test.ts` tests `unwrapChatbot` only on its own, and nothing imports the built package under Node ESM. (raised by 1/5 agents)
- VC-21: FAIL (suggestion) — notifyAttachmentListeners' doc says a listener that throws cannot stop the remaining listeners from being notified. [src/chat/ChatController.ts:237]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  ChatController.ts:238-246: each listener call is in try/catch, but the catch body calls console.error unguarded (line 243). Input: a listener that throws while console.error is replaced by a function that throws (or a console whose error is unavailable). The exception from console.error escapes the catch, leaves the for loop, and the remaining listeners are never notified. It also propagates to takeAttachments' caller. The doc says 'one that throws cannot stop the rest', which is absolute. It holds for the normal case, including a non-Error throw, which is just passed to console.error. It does not hold when the logger itself throws. The input is a hostile or odd environment, hence low severity. No external requirement source was shown, so this rests on the item's own source-authored claim.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (4)

<details><summary>4 items</summary>

- VC-18: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — react-chatbot-kit calls MessageParser.parse with the text the user submitted through its input, so `handleUserInput` marking turns `typed: true` covers exactly user-typed text and not text the kit or widget injects. [src/chat/ChatController.ts:254]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Repo side read: src/chat/ChatController.ts:515-517 MessageParser.parse(message) only calls controller.handleUserInput(message); the only references to MessageParser/createKitAdapters in src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx are lines 359 and 747 (passed as messageParser prop); nothing in src calls handleUserInput or parse directly for prefill/commands (open({command}) goes through runCommandInput). But the claim depends on where react-chatbot-kit's chat component calls messageParser.parse, and no dependency_sources were supplied and the library is not in head_view (Glob of view-head for **/react-chatbot-kit/** found nothing), so the kit's submit handler was not read from an allowed source.

  </details>

- VC-31: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — Handle calls through mount() run in the order they were made, including a call made after the ref attaches while earlier calls are still waiting in the queue for the pending flush. [src/mount.tsx:43]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  FAIL stored INCONCLUSIVE (requirement quote is missing): src/mount.tsx:43-46: withHandle runs action immediately whenever ref.current is set, without checking whether `queued` is non-empty. Trace: appendBlocks() while ref.current is null is pushed to queued (line 47) and flush scheduled via setTimeout 0 (line 64). React attaches the ref. open() is then called before the timer fires; ref.current is truthy, so open runs at line 44 immediately, ahead of the still-queued appendBlocks, which only runs at line 62 on flush. This reverses the call order, so the claim that calls run in the order made does not hold. A shipped caller (mount() consumers) can produce this sequence.

  </details>

- VC-33: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — After unmount(), calling update() on the returned object does not throw: it calls `root.render` on a root React has already unmounted, and React's behavior for that call is what determines the outcome. [src/mount.tsx:75]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  FAIL stored INCONCLUSIVE (requirement quote is missing): src/mount.tsx:75-83: update() calls render() -> root.render with no `unmounted` guard (other methods use withHandle, which checks it). unmount() calls root.unmount(). In node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js, unmount sets this._internalRoot = null (~line 31048), and render (line 31020) does `if (null === root) throw Error("Cannot update an unmounted root.")`. So update() after unmount() throws, contradicting the claim. Library version not checked; the source in node_modules is what was read.

  </details>

- VC-42: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — The comment asserts that until the Chatbot for the latest reset is mounted the controller is not bound to it and initialMessages seeds that mount; the code relies on createKitAdapters' ActionProvider binding the controller to the Chatbot keyed by chatResetKey no later than ChatWidget's layout effect at lines 492-494 records mountedResetKeyRef in the same commit, so equal mounted and requested keys mean controller.addMessages reaches the mounted Chatbot. [src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx:539]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Repo side read: ChatController.bind (ChatController.ts:198-200) just stores setState; addMessages->update uses this.setState?.() so it is a no-op when nothing is bound (203-209); the ActionProvider constructor binds only when setState is a function (506-512). ChatWidget.tsx:492-494 records mountedResetKeyRef in a layout effect, and appendBlocks (539-543) calls controller.addMessages only when mounted and requested keys are equal, else seeds initialMessages. The claim, however, depends on when react-chatbot-kit constructs the ActionProvider (during render, layout effect or passive effect) relative to ChatWidget's layout effect in the same commit, and on whether a stale setState survives unmount. The kit source is not in the views and no dependency_sources were supplied, so that timing cannot be established. Missing evidence: react-chatbot-kit's Chatbot/Chat source showing where `new ActionProvider(createChatBotMessage, setState, ...)` runs.

  </details>

</details>
